transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

This is a very common issue on Bosch heat-pump dryers like yours. The most likely cause is restricted airflow due to a blocked filter or condenser, which stops the machine from removing moisture effectively. Other possibilities include putting in laundry that was too wet from the washing machine, overloading the drum, or using a programme with a low dryness setting. To narrow this down, please check two things: 1) Is the lint filter in the door opening clean and intact? 2) Behind the small flap at the bottom left, is the condenser unit (the white plastic block with vertical fins) free of fluff and debris?

Door filter has fluff and a waxy film, and water barely passes through it when rinsed until I scrub it. Never cleaned the condenser before. When I took it out the front was matted with lint, I rinsed it with the shower head and it came clean.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. However, since the filter had a waxy film (likely from fabric softener), it may still have a thin residue that blocks air even if water runs through it. Also, if the sensor strips inside the drum are coated in softener, the dryer will think clothes are dry and stop too early. Please wipe those metal strips with vinegar to remove any coating, ensure the filter is bone-dry before refitting, and run a standard cotton cycle again.
Wiped the sensor bars with vinegar (they were slightly dull), and the filter's been rinsed and scrubbed. Anything else to do before I run a cycle?

Yes, just ensure the lint filter is bone-dry before refitting it; if any moisture remains on the mesh, it will block airflow. Also, make sure you are using a standard Cottons programme with full heat, as Eco modes run cooler and take much longer. Run one cycle now and let me know if the clothes come out significantly drier than before.
ok, will run a cottons cycle now and let you know how it goes

Good work getting those parts clean. Please run that cottons cycle now and let me know if the clothes come out significantly drier than before. If they are still damp, it suggests there is either a remaining blockage in the condenser airflow or the sensors are not reading correctly despite the cleaning.
Ran the cottons cycle. Clothes dry in about 100 minutes and the water container is nearly full now, so much better.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That is excellent news. The combination of a blocked lint filter and the uncleaned condenser was most likely restricting the airflow needed for efficient drying. To keep it running well, try to clean the condenser every few months and avoid using too much fabric softener, which causes that waxy buildup on the sensors and filters. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
